text:
Both responses are accurate on the core facts: no external access, 347 members affected, no passwords or card numbers, the job stopped before the remaining 11,200 statements went out, the regulator notified on 3 October, members contacted by 6 October, and the 9 October resend. Response B adds that the job "was stopped after 35 minutes," but the report gives only the 9:35am stop time, not when the job started, so that figure is unsupported. Response A has no such error. Response A also covers the premature "we've been hacked" all-staff message and its leak to local news, which a manager would want to know about and which Response B omits. However, Response A runs to roughly 160 words, breaking the explicit under-120-word limit, while Response B stays at about 110. Weighing accuracy first, Response A is the better summary despite the length overrun, though the word limit keeps this from being a clear-cut call.

Verdict: A
